items.summary: INTEGRATED PHOTONIC MICROROBOTIC SYSTEMS AT THE LIMIT FLAGSHIP 16 / 30 | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXIV This prospective research monograph investigates whether silicon-photonic light distribution, optofluidic packaging, independent metrology, and feedback positioning can be integrated into a compact research station that reliably captures, transports, releases, and recovers microscopic proxy agents. Its central hypothesis is system-level rather than decorative: reducing external optics is a meaningful advance only when delivered optical power, fluid transport, sample heating, task outcomes, and failure responses remain independently observable and reproducible across fabricated chip and package lots. The study develops a five-layer research architecture encompassing packaged optical and fluidic paths; a physically bounded optical-power and thermal ledger; external tracking capable of challenging on-chip estimates; reversible multi-agent tasks under staged fault injection; and repair, requalification, cost, and cross-laboratory transfer. It separates electromagnetic optical force from thermal convection, surface adhesion, Brownian motion, and sensor-induced artefacts. Strong comparators include calibrated free-space optical tweezers and spatial-light-modulator trapping configurations at matched specimen exposure and operational throughput. The book contains 30 mathematics-linked derivational routes, 82 chapters with 410 independently paginated research sections, 200 detailed future Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A companion Excel atlas links each research chapter, quantitative candidate, test protocol, falsifier and external DOI evidence record. Publisher-identified publications on integrated optical phased arrays, silicon-photonic trapping, and photonics packaging inform the research boundary but are not treated as proof that the integrated microrobotic platform proposed here has already been demonstrated. The primary design principle is independent reproducibility: a controller should never be allowed to certify its own sensor output, ignore lost agents, or authorize a restart after a failed optical-power or thermal ledger. Negative studies, matched classical successes, and failed module integrations are retained as useful successor research evidence. This work offers testable possibilities for future investigation; it is not a claim of experimentally demonstrated autonomous nanorobots, and it has not undergone external peer review.

items.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.
items.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses

items.summary: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) have extended their capabilities beyond lexical speech understanding to tasks requiring paralinguistic and non-linguistic audio understanding, such as emotion recognition. However, these models still struggle to reliably utilize acoustic information, particularly when it co-occurs with spoken linguistic content. Existing benchmarks do not clearly distinguish acoustic perception from higher-level reasoning, making it difficult to identify the source of these failures. To address this issue, we introduce VocalGrad, a benchmark designed to evaluate LALMs' ability to perceive low-level acoustic variations. VocalGrad formulates this problem as a simple binary classification of temporal change direction, enabling evaluation largely independent of higher-level reasoning or semantic understanding. Our benchmark results reveal a substantial gap in acoustic perception between human annotators and state-of-the-art LALMs: while human annotators achieve high accuracy, LALMs perform at near-chance levels. We further conduct linear probing to identify structural bottlenecks in these models. Our analysis reveals two distinct failure modes: for some categories, task-relevant information is preserved in internal representations but not utilized by the language model head; for others, the information becomes progressively less linearly decodable across model layers. Overall, our results reveal substantial limitations of LALMs in modeling acoustic variation under controlled settings and expose representation differences not observable from text outputs.
items.title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models

items.summary: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.
items.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness

items.summary: Emergency-stop circuits built by engineering technology students are routinely treated as safe once they pass a functional test at commissioning, yet the relay contact welding that dominates their failure modes is invisible to such tests and accumulates silently across the workshop's operating life. The framework represents a student-built circuit as a series safety function whose integrity is degraded by contact welding, and derives the conditions under which a welded contact converts a demanded stop into an undetected loss of safety function. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator was conducted under a declared variance structure with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The evaluation indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect at 80% power falls as the number of clusters rises. The framework proposes that workshop safety assurance should shift from commissioning-time functional testing to integrity monitoring that is sensitive to contact welding, and the design analysis implies that cluster-level evaluations of such interventions require cluster counts well above those typical of single-institution studies.

items.summary: Finite-element models, extracted results, analysis scripts and figure scripts supporting the article "Competing Failure Modes in Residually Stressed Thin Films on Flexible Substrates: Wrinkling, Channel Cracking, and Their Coupling" (International Journal of Solids and Structures). All finite-element calculations are carried out with ABAQUS/Standard 2021: the plane-strain linear-buckling benchmark and the geometrically nonlinear post-buckling sweep (imperfection, phase and mesh), the channel-crack factor and stress field, the J-integral and cohesive-zone crest-crack models, the three-dimensional stripe, checkerboard, hexagonal and herringbone wrinkle patterns, and the Al/Al2O3 equi-biaxial unit cell. The archive contains the input-generation scripts, input files, ODB post-processing scripts, results in JSON format, solver logs, the Python scripts that reproduce Figures 1–17 of the article, the figures, a README, a figure-to-source map, software versions and a SHA-256 file manifest. The three zip files unpack into one folder, thin_film_failure_modes_data.
items.title: Data and code for "Competing Failure Modes in Residually Stressed Thin Films on Flexible Substrates: Wrinkling, Channel Cracking, and Their Coupling"

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode: a goal-directed builder and an exists-forall search, each followed by an independent gate. From the rules of Steinberg's problem it rebuilds the gadgets of the 2016 counterexample of Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado; it finds nothing on Erdős's question for cycles of length 4 to 6. Layer towers of depth one to three, a ladder and a mesh, are compared with the crossing loop at the same number of checks. A Hodge-only run of twelve rounds leaves every target point at the same gap. None of the five benchmark problems (the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture, Erdős problem 1183) is solved. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.
items.title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

items.summary: We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(χ(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). By gluing two blocks formed by \(G_2/SU(3)\cong S^6\) and the unit disk $D(V)$ of 12- dimensional real $S^1$-representation $V$ along their equivariantly identified free boundaries, we explicitly construct such a manifold $M^{18}_3$. We also prove that the four-point case is null-bordant in real dimension \(16\) and in every real dimension greater than \(18\); hence \(18\) is the smallest dimension in which such a counterexample occurs.
items.title: Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture

items.summary: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. Despite this progress, success rates remain low, and it is unclear which capability these fine-tuned policies lack. Our diagnosis identifies goal grounding as the dominant failure. These policies explore well, yet often fail to notice that the goal is already in view or to estimate how far away it is. To address this failure, we ground the goal explicitly. Explicit grounding substantially improves success and reaches state-of-the-art results on six benchmarks across three scene collections. We also correct annotation defects in these benchmarks, so that future methods are evaluated more faithfully. Our analysis on the clean benchmarks shows that, with ground-truth grounding, our policy nearly matches the expert that generated its demonstrations, leaving the headroom in perception rather than policy learning. Our work points to goal grounding as a missing piece of object-goal navigation and offers a simple and effective solution to the task.
items.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation

items.summary: Diffusion-based multimodal large language models (dMLLMs) decode by iterative denoising with bidirectional attention, which precludes the standard autoregressive key--value cache. Practical deployments therefore rely on approximate caching that reuses intermediate states across denoising steps. Such caching, however, often makes a response repeat one token at adjacent positions in a run that breaks the sentence, a failure we term the \emph{Repeat Curse}. Tracing the context-token information flow reveals three disruptions. Within a step, caching disperses the attention that anchors a position on nearby context tokens. Across steps, similarity-based refresh is not staleness-aware, so some positions are decoded against stale key--value states. Across layers, the deep-layer entropy of the context fails to converge where repetition arises. items.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. items.summary: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. Despite this progress, success rates remain low, and it is unclear which capability these fine-tuned policies lack. Our diagnosis identifies goal grounding as the dominant failure. These policies explore well, yet often fail to notice that the goal is already in view or to estimate how far away it is. To address this failure, we ground the goal explicitly. Explicit grounding substantially improves success and reaches state-of-the-art results on six benchmarks across three scene collections. We also correct annotation defects in these benchmarks, so that future methods are evaluated more faithfully. Our analysis on the clean benchmarks shows that, with ground-truth grounding, our policy nearly matches the expert that generated its demonstrations, leaving the headroom in perception rather than policy learning. Our work points to goal grounding as a missing piece of object-goal navigation and offers a simple and effective solution to the task.

items.summary: Relational out-of-distribution errors are easy to describe and hard to evaluate cleanly. An image may be natural, a caption may be fluent, and all mentioned objects may be common, yet the caption may describe the wrong relation in the image. Many evaluations intended to test this behavior can be solved without checking the pairing at all, because negatives differ in caption style, template, length, object frequency, or image statistics. We propose counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same two images and the same two captions on both sides of the comparison, changing only which image is paired with which caption. This makes image-only, text-only, and additive component shortcuts cancel exactly in finite samples. The same contrast also gives a training loss for relational outlier exposure and a diagnostic for bilinear vision-language scores. Across synthetic controls, GQA, and COCO, cycles separate coarse image-caption matching from directional role-binding failures, while also identifying geometric size relations that remain strongly visible in global features. In a shortcut-contaminated COCO outlier-exposure stress test, a model selected by a near-perfect shortcut validation AUROC retains substantial relational signal but remains below cycle training on exact cycles; cycle training improves CycleAcc from 0.882 to 0.927. The main lesson is simple: to test whether a model understands a pairing, the benchmark should keep the parts fixed, change the pairing, and ask only about coupling. The official implementation is available online.

items.summary: Physical plausibility is essential for realistic video generation. Existing methods impose physical guidance before synthesis via simulations or refined prompts, but this can limit dynamic diversity, miss errors that emerge only after generation, and require repeated regeneration when inconsistencies remain. We therefore study a generate-diagnose-repair paradigm that preserves the original generation capability and selectively repairs physical inconsistencies afterward, raising two key questions: what to repair and how to repair? To address them, we introduce PhysRepair, an agentic video generation framework that combines causal reasoning over the observed physical failure with prior repair experience to enable localized and adaptive correction. Specifically, Spatiotemporal Causal Constraints identify the first invalid physical state and its causally affected states, producing a repair specification that guides physically plausible local regeneration while preserving unaffected content. Experience-augmented In-context Learning combines the ongoing repair context with relevant experience from previous repairs, allowing the agent to adapt its repair decisions across diverse physical failures and accumulate completed trajectories for future cases. Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods. Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.
items.title: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning

items.summary: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) and ischaemia with non-obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA) are increasingly recognised syndromes in which endothelial dysfunction forms the mechanistic bridge between vascular biology and clinical ischaemia. In health, the endothelium preserves vascular homeostasis by regulating tone, platelet activity, and inflammation; when this regulation fails, vessels assume a pro-constrictive, pro-thrombotic, and pro-inflammatory state capable of causing epicardial vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, or plaque erosion—provoking genuine infarction and arrhythmias despite unobstructed arteries. This paper follows the continuum from these mechanisms to their clinical expression. It traces the evolution from early angiographic observations to contemporary imaging such as CMR, IVUS, and OCT, and outlines a chronological diagnostic pathway from the emergency department to the catheterisation laboratory. Subtle but actionable clues are highlighted across the clinical history, ECG, echocardiography, and angiography, demonstrating that a positive, mechanism-based diagnosis of endothelial dysfunction is feasible even when invasive testing is unavailable. Management is directed by the dominant mechanism calcium-channel blockers and nitrates for vasospastic angina; β-blockers or metabolic agents for microvascular angina supported by endothelial stabilisers, cardiac rehabilitation, and psychosocial care. Persistent endothelial dysfunction is associated with later heart-failure development, particularly HFpEF, emphasising the need     for   early   recognition     and     tailored   therapy.   The  chapter concludes with real-world challenges and emerging perspectives, including standardised testing, AI-assisted imaging, and precision therapeutics. Ultimately, understanding endothelial dysfunction links mechanisms to clinical practice, reframing MINOCA and INOCA as diagnosable and treatable syndromes that demand mechanism-based, preventive care.

items.summary: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason. The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts. Our Perception-Memory Fidelity (PMF) Gap-guided OPD-RL framework dynamically balances privileged distillation and task-reward optimization, with periodic teacher updates supporting continued improvement. We further introduce ECHOESBMK, a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark derived from real GUI agent failure trajectories to jointly evaluate visual perception and cross-modal state retention. Experiments on four GUI benchmarks and ECHOESBMK demonstrate substantial gains in task performance and memory fidelity. Without retaining historical screenshots at deployment, ECHOES achieves competitive performance with a favorable performance-inference-cost trade-off and exhibits positive zero-shot transfer to unseen visual planning tasks.
items.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation

items.summary: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 allows a child aged sixteen or seventeen who is alleged to have committed a heinous offence to be tried as an adult after a "preliminary assessment" by the Juvenile Justice Board. This paper argues that the transfer mechanism is less a principled answer to serious adolescent offending than a legislative compromise whose costs fall on the procedural guarantees the Act otherwise extends to children. It reads section 15 against the Supreme Court's decisions in Shilpa Mittal and Barun Chandra Thakur, the age-determination case law, and the developmental research on adolescent culpability, and it engages the retributive and victim-centred case for transfer on its own terms. Accountability and rehabilitation, the paper contends, are not two poles to be traded off at a single age threshold. Both depend on institutional capacity that the system has never been resourced to supply: functioning Boards, trained probation staff, individual care plans that are actually followed, and aftercare that reaches young people beyond eighteen. Reform should narrow and proceduralise transfer, introduce statutory diversion, decouple offence classification from the general penal code, and treat implementation failure as a rights violation rather than an administrative shortfall.

items.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have significantly advanced instruction-driven perception through the "Embedding-as-Mask" paradigm. However, extending this capability to Remote Sensing (RS) reasoning segmentation remains exceptionally challenging under cluttered geographical contexts and extreme scale variations, often leading to Spatial Fidelity Degradation and Target Misidentification. We identify a critical yet underexplored bottleneck: the sequential alienation of the segmentation token [SEG] from its initial visual grounding within the autoregressive generation paradigm. Produced only at the end of long reasoning chains, [SEG] relies on visual evidence that has been progressively diluted by linguistic abstraction and autoregressive noise. This information decay is particularly catastrophic for RS targets with minuscule pixel footprints, where even marginal fidelity loss leads to localization failure. To address these bottlenecks, we propose GeoReason, a novel framework designed to fortify logical deduction and preserve spatial integrity. First, we introduce an Anticipatory Prior mechanism that injects the [SEG] token directly into the initial user query, shifting it from a terminal output to a primary condition. This paradigm shift transforms the token into a persistent spatial anchor, preventing information decay during long-form linguistic inference. Second, we enhance visual reasoning via a Location-aware Chain-of-Thought (CoT) that enforces coarse-to-fine localization using bounding boxes, coupled with a Latent Patch-to-Token Alignment (PTA) Loss that explicitly aligns the latent segmentation token with physical RS textures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GeoReason consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the Earthreason and RRSIS-D benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Fanc0126/GeoReason.
items.title: GeoReason: Bridging Logical Reasoning and Spatial Fidelity in Remote Sensing Segmentation

items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: INTEGRATED PHOTONIC MICROROBOTIC SYSTEMS AT THE LIMIT FLAGSHIP 16 / 30 | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXIV This prospective research monograph investigates whether silicon-photonic light distribution, optofluidic packaging, independent metrology, and feedback positioning can be integrated into a compact research station that reliably captures, transports, releases, and recovers microscopic proxy agents. Its central hypothesis is system-level rather than decorative: reducing external optics is a meaningful advance only when delivered optical power, fluid transport, sample heating, task outcomes, and failure responses remain independently observable and reproducible across fabricated chip and package lots. The study develops a five-layer research architecture encompassing packaged optical and fluidic paths; a physically bounded optical-power and thermal ledger; external tracking capable of challenging on-chip estimates; reversible multi-agent tasks under staged fault injection; and repair, requalification, cost, and cross-laboratory transfer. It separates electromagnetic optical force from thermal convection, surface adhesion, Brownian motion, and sensor-induced artefacts. Strong comparators include calibrated free-space optical tweezers and spatial-light-modulator trapping configurations at matched specimen exposure and operational throughput. The book contains 30 mathematics-linked derivational routes, 82 chapters with 410 independently paginated research sections, 200 detailed future Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A companion Excel atlas links each research chapter, quantitative candidate, test protocol, falsifier and external DOI evidence record. Publisher-identified publications on integrated optical phased arrays, silicon-photonic trapping, and photonics packaging inform the research boundary but are not treated as proof that the integrated microrobotic platform proposed here has already been demonstrated. The primary design principle is independent reproducibility: a controller should never be allowed to certify its own sensor output, ignore lost agents, or authorize a restart after a failed optical-power or thermal ledger. Negative studies, matched classical successes, and failed module integrations are retained as useful successor research evidence. This work offers testable possibilities for future investigation; it is not a claim of experimentally demonstrated autonomous nanorobots, and it has not undergone external peer review.

Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods. Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.

items.summary: Laser cladding enables bi-material components with tailored surface properties, but cyclic loading makes fatigue resistance of the whole component critical. This study examined the bending fatigue life (R = 0.1) of unalloyed steels S235J2 and S355J2 and high-strength steels S460NL and S690QL clad with aluminium bronze Metco 51NS, a combination typical of tube-bending mandrels. Results were evaluated as force amplitude versus cycles to failure using a Basquin-type power law. Fatigue strength at 10⁷ cycles was 4.0, 3.4, 3.8 and 4.5 kN, respectively, so high-strength steels performed only slightly better or similarly. Cracks always initiated on the surface of the cladding and crossed the defect-free interface. The base material is therefore not decisive for fatigue life, which is governed by the surface layer, provided cladding parameters are optimal. Less expensive unalloyed steels are thus sufficient for such components.
items.title: Fatigue resistance of structural steels coated with aluminium bronze using laser cladding

items.summary: LLM agents increasingly use retrieval tools across languages, yet their safety evaluation remains English-centric. It remains unclear whether language affects tool admission, post-retrieval generation, or both. We independently vary request, retrieved-page, and required response languages in a controlled URL-retrieval setting across ten models and seven languages. We identify Safety Loss through Interlingual Processing (SLIP). Non-English harmful requests increase mean tool admission from 46.9% to 67.4%, with a positive mean change in every model. This pattern also persists in an autonomous retrieval setup across all four models tested in this setting. Requiring answers in the page language increases pooled harmfulness on matched tool calls from 50.3% to 57.4% across four closed-weight models, mainly in Chinese and Hindi. Translating pages alone produces no consistent harm increase in eight models with comparable inference settings. Automated audits show that a non-harmful response may be a genuine safety refusal, a deflection citing language difficulties, or an unusable answer. Harmfulness labels alone cannot distinguish these outcomes. Multilingual safety evaluations should therefore measure tool admission and response harmfulness separately and distinguish refusal from capability failure.
items.title: Disentangling Language Effects on Tool Admission and Post-Retrieval Safety

items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: We develop a counterfactual semantics based on reopening partial information states. Evaluation first removes enough stated content to leave the antecedent’s attributes unresolved, retaining what the chosen scope protects, then asserts the antecedent and considers the surviving consistent refinements. Would and might quantify over the admissible alternatives; a weighted extension supplies graded evaluations. The principal result concerns finite models with fully supported residues. When a conjunctive antecedent reopens each constituent attribute, adding a supported conjunct can remove the grounds of another conclusion. A four-attribute countermodel therefore violates Cautious Monotony, excluding any smooth preferential representation that preserves the evaluable verdicts. We also establish a sufficient nesting condition for Cut and exhibit its failure without that condition. The conjunctive reopening rule is an explicit interpretive commitment; its suitability for ordinary-language counterfactuals remains an empirical question. The account uses declared dependencies, scope restrictions, and priorities, while the quantitative extension assumes a weight kernel. Comparisons with belief revision, premise semantics, update semantics, and causal intervention identify the consequences of reopening an attribute rather than merely making its proposed value consistent with retained information.
items.title: Counterfactual Evaluation by Reopening Information States

items.summary: Speculative decoding typically characterizes speedup by draft tokens accepted per verification round. Lossless verification preserves the target model's output distribution and thus expected completion length, making this metric a meaningful efficiency proxy. Relaxed (lossy) verification accepts tokens that lossless verification would reject, potentially altering that distribution. We identify a length inflation phenomenon: relaxed verification lengthens completions, primarily by extending reasoning traces, largely offsetting apparent gains in accepted tokens per round. We evaluate existing training-free relaxed verification rules on twelve target-drafter pairs against lossless verification on identical prompts, measuring completion length, verifier rounds, wall-clock time, and task accuracy. At each rule's most relaxed evaluated setting, relaxed verification on average accepts $1.34\times$ as many tokens per round but produces $1.54\times$ longer completions. For rules with higher acceptance lengths, tokens accepted only under relaxed verification tend to have low target-model probability, contributing to length inflation. For rules that reduce verifier rounds, accuracy typically drops substantially. Further analysis traces some failures to continued reasoning that exhausts the budget needed to deliver a final answer. Overall, accepted tokens per round alone is an unreliable measure of decoding speed under relaxed verification. Completion length and verifier rounds must also be reported to assess actual efficiency.
items.title: Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding

items.summary: Relational out-of-distribution errors are easy to describe and hard to evaluate cleanly. An image may be natural, a caption may be fluent, and all mentioned objects may be common, yet the caption may describe the wrong relation in the image. Many evaluations intended to test this behavior can be solved without checking the pairing at all, because negatives differ in caption style, template, length, object frequency, or image statistics. We propose counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same two images and the same two captions on both sides of the comparison, changing only which image is paired with which caption. This makes image-only, text-only, and additive component shortcuts cancel exactly in finite samples. The same contrast also gives a training loss for relational outlier exposure and a diagnostic for bilinear vision-language scores. Across synthetic controls, GQA, and COCO, cycles separate coarse image-caption matching from directional role-binding failures, while also identifying geometric size relations that remain strongly visible in global features. In a shortcut-contaminated COCO outlier-exposure stress test, a model selected by a near-perfect shortcut validation AUROC retains substantial relational signal but remains below cycle training on exact cycles; cycle training improves CycleAcc from 0.882 to 0.927. The main lesson is simple: to test whether a model understands a pairing, the benchmark should keep the parts fixed, change the pairing, and ask only about coupling. The official implementation is available online.
items.title: Can the Parts Fool the Test? Counterfactual Pairing Cycles for Relational OOD

items.summary: Notes cover the changes since 0.5.0. pip install metabeta==0.6.0 Tutorials Three notebooks in demos/ replace intro.ipynb and priors.ipynb . Each runs on a CPU runtime in Colab. 01-quickstart : lme4's sleepstudy end to end, next to lme4's estimates. 02-families : Bernoulli ( cbpp ) and Poisson ( Salamanders ) fits, posterior predictive checks, and random-walk moves next to a NUTS reference. 03-priors : prior specification, prior sensitivity in one call, and model comparison by Bayes factors. New reports posteriorDraws(result) : posterior draws of the global parameters on the data's scale, as a DataFrame named as in posteriorSummary (#31). groupDraws(result) : each group's coefficients per draw, the fixed effect plus the group's deviation (#33). posteriorPredictive(result) : the observed responses and one replicate per posterior draw, in the data's units (#33). bayesFactor(result, reference) : the Bayes factor of one model over another, per prior, with its Kass–Raftery grade; both results come from sample(evidence=True) (#33). sample n_samples defaults to 1,000 draws (#19). seed= makes a call reproducible and leaves the caller's random stream untouched (#32). posteriorPredictive and plotPPD take seed= too (#26, #33). Every summary ends with a fit metric: R² (Gaussian), AUC (Bernoulli) or deviance (Poisson) (#29). loo=True adds PSIS-LOO to the summary; it replaces diagnostics=True (#29). random_walk=True runs silently and warns only below an IMH effective sample size (ESS) of 10 (#29). Warnings state the failure, its consequence and numbered remedies, and point at the user's call (#18, #29). The first call after loading costs about as much as a warm one; warmup() runs that pass explicitly (#19). Formulas, scales and names Formulas follow lme4: y ~ 1 + (1 | g) fits an intercept-only model, preprocessing reads only the columns the formula names, and column names keep their case (#15). The order of fixed terms no longer changes the fit; names are mapped back in every output (#16). Summaries default to x_scale='original' . Random-effect SDs, correlations and per-group effects are on the data's scale like the fixed effects, and so are the prior lines (#17). rfxSummary labels each group correctly (#17). Api.from_pretrained('gaussian') is an alias of 'normal' , in any case (#30). Reports pick a dataset row by prior_id , a prior's name or its index (#32). Errors Unsupported formula syntax raises NotImplementedError with a workaround: || , nested or crossed grouping factors, interactions ( : , * ) and function calls such as log() or factor() (#18). Data outside every submodel's range raises one ValueError that names the limits; a family mismatch names the checkpoint to load (#18). A named predictor dropped as collinear or near-constant raises an error that names it (#18). Formulas the pretrained models cannot fit raise an error that names the fix: a random intercept without a fixed one, or the reverse, and a random slope that is not a fixed term (#16). GPU from_pretrained(..., device='cuda') works on GPUs whose torch build lacks a cholesky_solve kernel, such as Colab's T4 with torch 2.11 for CUDA 13 (#26). plotParameters and sample(loo=True) work on a CUDA device (#26). Packaging Python 3.13 support, with dependency floors at Colab's preinstalled versions (#20). The code is licensed under Apache-2.0, previously CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (#21). CITATION.cff drives GitHub's citation button (#21). Deprecated, removed in 0.7 Each alias still works and raises a FutureWarning (#29, #32). sample(diagnostics=True) : use loo=True . batch_index= in posteriorSummary and rfxSummary , and index= in plotParameters : use prior_id= . indices= in plotPPD : use prior_ids= .
items.title: metabeta: amortized Bayesian inference for generalized linear mixed-effects models
